title: Solutions: Algorithmic Challenges
section: A bounding box is four numbers
text:
A bounding box is four numbers

The axis-aligned bounding box of a set of points is the smallest rectangle (with sides parallel to the axes) that contains all of them
Numerically: just four values

\[\text{BB} = (x_{\min},\ y_{\min},\ x_{\max},\ y_{\max})\]

Key insight: you never need to store the full point list — only the current extremes

title: Solutions: Algorithmic Challenges
Solutions: Algorithmic Challenges
text:
R implementation

stream <- matrix(c(
  2489750, 1117500,
  2506250, 1172500,
  2552750, 1223500,
  2498000, 1198000,
  2470000, 1145000
), ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE)

bb <- c(xmin = stream[1,1], xmax = stream[1,1],
        ymin = stream[1,2], ymax = stream[1,2])

for (i in seq_len(nrow(stream))) {
  bb["xmin"] <- min(bb["xmin"], stream[i, 1])
  bb["xmax"] <- max(bb["xmax"], stream[i, 1])
  bb["ymin"] <- min(bb["ymin"], stream[i, 2])
  bb["ymax"] <- max(bb["ymax"], stream[i, 2])
}

title: Solutions: Algorithmic Challenges
text:
The intuition
Draw a ray from the point horizontally to the right (→ infinity):

Count how many polygon edges the ray crosses
Odd number of crossings → point is inside
Even number of crossings → point is outside

title: Solutions: Algorithmic Challenges
text:
Ray casting: the algorithm
For each edge of the polygon (vertex \(i\) → vertex \(i+1\)):

Does the edge straddle the horizontal line \(y = p_y\)? \[( y_i > p_y ) \ne ( y_{i+1} > p_y )\]
If yes: is the ray–edge intersection to the right of \(p_x\)? \[x_{\text{hit}} = x_i + \frac{(p_y - y_i)(x_{i+1} - x_i)}{y_{i+1} - y_i} > p_x\]
If both conditions hold → flip an inside boolean (starts FALSE)

Result: inside after all edges = TRUE if the point is inside.

title: Solutions: Algorithmic Challenges
text:
R implementation

point_in_poly <- function(px, py, vx, vy) {
  n <- length(vx)
  inside <- FALSE
  j <- n
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    if (((vy[i] > py) != (vy[j] > py)) &&
        (px < (vx[j] - vx[i]) * (py - vy[i]) / (vy[j] - vy[i]) + vx[i])) {
      inside <- !inside
    }
    j <- i
  }
  inside
}

# polygon: a rough triangle
vx <- c(1, 4, 2.5); vy <- c(1, 1, 4)

point_in_poly(2.5, 2,   vx, vy)  # inside  → TRUE

[1] TRUE

point_in_poly(0,   0,   vx, vy)  # outside → FALSE

[1] FALSE

point_in_poly(3.5, 3.5, vx, vy)  # outside → FALSE

[1] FALSE

title: Solutions: Algorithmic Challenges
text:
Edge cases







Situation
How to handle




Ray passes exactly through a vertex
Use strict > on one side, >= on the other — ensures each vertex is counted at most once


Point lies exactly on an edge
Technically undefined; most implementations return TRUE


Polygon is not closed
Close it: ensure last vertex = first vertex


Concave / complex polygons
Algorithm works unchanged — this is its strength over simpler methods

title: Geocomputation with Vector Data
text:
Why a standard?

Vector data is used in PostGIS, QGIS, R, Python, ArcGIS, GDAL, …
Simple Features (ISO 19125-1:2004) is the OGC standard all major spatial tools implement
It defines: geometry types, encoding, and spatial relationships

title: Geocomputation with Vector Data
text:
What is a feature?

A simple feature is defined […] to have both spatial and non-spatial attributes. Spatial attributes are geometry valued, and simple features are based on 2D geometry with linear interpolation between vertices.

— ISO 19125

title: Geocomputation with Vector Data
text:
Geometry types

18 types defined in the standard; 7 cover the vast majority of real-world data:





Table 1: Source: Pebesma (2018)











Type
Description
Dimensions




POINT
zero-dimensional geometry containing a single point
0


LINESTRING
sequence of points connected by straight, non-self-intersecting line pieces
1


POLYGON
sequence of points forming a closed, non-self-intersecting ring (with optional holes)
2


MULTIPOINT
set of points
0


MULTILINESTRING
set of linestrings
1


MULTIPOLYGON
set of polygons
2

set of geometries of any of the above types

title: Geocomputation with Vector Data
text:
The Earth is not flat

The Earth is approximated as an ellipsoid: slightly flattened at the poles, bulging at the equator
A datum defines which ellipsoid to use and how to orient it:

WGS84 — global datum, used by GPS and internet maps
CH1903+ / LV95 — Swiss national datum, optimized for Switzerland

The same point has different coordinates in different datums

title: Geocomputation with Vector Data
text:
Projections

A projection transforms 3D ellipsoid coordinates onto a flat 2D plane
Every projection distorts at least one property — there is no undistorted flat map:

Equal-area — preserves area; distorts shape and angles
Conformal — preserves local shape / angles; distorts area
Equidistant — preserves distance from a point; distorts area and shape

National systems (e.g. LV95 / EPSG:2056) are conformal, minimizing distortion locally

GDAL: one library, many tools

GDAL (Geospatial Data Abstraction Library) underlies almost all GIS software:

QGIS, ArcGIS, GRASS, SAGA, FME, …
R (sf)
Python (geopandas)
PostGIS



# sf delegates format detection to GDAL — driver chosen from file extension
stationen <- read_sf("data/uebung1/stationen_schweiz.geojson")   # → GeoJSON driver
hoheitsgebiet <- read_sf("data/Spatial_Analysis_I/Hoheitsgebiet/HOHEITSGEBIET_FR.shp")  # → Shapefile driver


GDAL supports 80+ vector formats; sf inherits all of them

title: Geocomputation with Vector Data
text:
Spatial relationships as questions

Binary predicates return TRUE/FALSE for a pair of geometries
The question determines the correct predicate:

Is this building inside the flood zone? → st_within(building, zone)
Does this road cross the zone? → st_crosses(road, zone)
Does any part of this forest touch Luzern? → st_intersects(forest, luzern)

The same pair can satisfy multiple predicates — wrong choice gives silently wrong results

title: Geocomputation with Vector Data
text:
Named predicates









Predicate

When TRUE
Typical use case




intersects

Any overlap exists (broadest)
Initial spatial filter


disjoint

No overlap whatsoever
Exclusion / NOT queries


touches

Boundaries meet; interiors do not
Adjacent parcels, shared borders





intersects is almost always TRUE for non-trivial pairs — rarely the right predicate for a precise question

title: Geocomputation with Vector Data
text:
Choosing the right predicate

# intersects: any part of the forest touches Luzern (including tiny overlap at the border)
wald_intersects <- st_filter(tlm_wald, luzern, .predicate = st_intersects)

# within: the *entire* forest polygon lies inside Luzern
wald_within <- st_filter(tlm_wald, luzern, .predicate = st_within)

nrow(wald_intersects)  # more: includes forests that merely touch the border

[1] 3852

nrow(wald_within)      # fewer: only forests completely inside

[1] 3729

Unary operations

Take one geometry, return a (possibly different type of) geometry:









Operation
What it does
Output type




st_buffer(x, dist)
Expand by distance
Polygon


st_centroid(x)
Center point
Point


st_simplify(x, tol)
Reduce vertex count
Same type


st_convex_hull(x)
Smallest convex polygon enclosing the geometry

st_boundary(x)

title: Geocomputation with Vector Data
text:
Binary set operations

Set algebra on geometries — same logic as SQL set operations
st_union() on a single layer: dissolve / aggregate — analogous to GROUP BY in SQL




Operation
Returns
Set notation




st_intersection(A, B)
Parts where A and B overlap
A ∩ B


st_union(A, B)
All of A and B, merged
A ∪ B


st_difference(A, B)
Parts of A outside B
A  B


st_sym_difference(A, B)
Parts of A or B, but not both
A △ B

title: Geocomputation with Vector Data
text:
Operations can change geometry type

Output type depends on the geometry relationship, not just the operation
Intersecting two polygons can yield a polygon, a line, or a point:

Overlapping → polygon;
sharing only an edge → line;
sharing only a corner → point

Code expecting a polygon fails silently if inputs only touch

section: Challenge 1: Bounding box of a point stream
text:
Challenge 1: Bounding box of a point stream


A continuous stream of 2D coordinates arrives one point at a time.
Task: develop an algorithm for the smallest axis-aligned bounding box of all points received so far.
Constraints: process each point once; do not store the full list; update the box on each new point.
Example stream:
2489750, 1117500
2506250, 1172500
2552750, 1223500  ...








Closed book!


Do not use any external sources. Solve with your own ideas in groups

title: Geocomputation with Vector Data
section: Challenge 2: Is a point inside a polygon?
text:
Challenge 2: Is a point inside a polygon?


Given: an ordered sequence of 2D polygon vertices and a point with known coordinates.
Task: develop an algorithm that determines whether the point is inside or outside the polygon.
Constraints: use only the vertex coordinates; no visual inspection; must work for arbitrary simple polygons.








Closed book!


Do not use any external sources. Solve with your own ideas in groups

title: Vector Data
text:
Scenario 1: Protected Area Planning
Analyse wetland ecosystems to inform nature protection planning.

1.1: How much wetland area (“Feuchtgebiet”) exists in Canton Luzern (km²)?
1.2: Identify wetlands within 50m of standing water (“Stehende Gewaesser”). What percentage of total wetland area does this represent?
1.3: Map all wetlands, water-connected wetlands (highlighted), and standing water bodies.

title: Vector Data
text:
Scenario 2: Accessibility Analysis
Analyse forest accessibility for a hiking organisation.

2.1: How much forest area in Luzern is within 200m of small paths (“1m Weg”, “2m Weg”)?
2.2: What percentage of total forest area does this represent?
2.3: Compare with accessibility by major roads (Autobahn, Autostrasse, streets ≥6m).
2.4: Map your findings.

title: Vector Data
text:
Scenario 3: Alpine Environment Analysis
Analyse high-altitude land cover for climate research.

3.1: Combine all rocky types (“Fels”, “Fels locker”, “Felsbloecke”, “Felsbloecke locker”, “Lockergestein”). What is their total area?
3.2: Find rocky areas within 100m of glaciers (“Gletscher”) or snow fields (“Schneefeld Toteis”). What share does this represent?
3.3: Map rocky areas, rocky areas near ice/snow, and glaciers/snow fields.

title: Vector Data
text:
Scenario 4: Integrated Analysis
Identify potential sites for small agricultural reservoirs. Suitable areas must meet all of:

Within 20m of wetlands
Within 300m of any road
Not in forest
Not on rocky terrain (“Fels”, “Felsbloecke”)

Map suitable areas and report the total area.
